instruction:
In the container, repository at /dayjs (a dayjs checkout). Do NOT modify any files. Investigate and report facts only.

Task: run the existing test suite and report which tests pass/fail BEFORE any edits. Specifically:
1. cd /dayjs && npx jest --coverage=false 2>&1 | tail -60   (report pass/fail counts and names of any failing tests)
2. cd /dayjs && TZ=Pacific/Auckland npx jest test/timezone.test --coverage=false 2>&1 | tail -30
3. Report the node version (node -v), and whether `Intl.DateTimeFormat` with timeZone works.
Also report the output of `cd /dayjs && git log --oneline -15` and `git status --short`.
Report exact command outputs (trimmed) in your final report.

You are working in the container in the repository /dayjs (a dayjs checkout, jest + babel test setup). Your job: apply ONE small source fix and verify it. Do NOT touch any file under /dayjs/test except creating (and later deleting) the temporary test file described below. Do not modify any other source file.

BACKGROUND: /dayjs/src/plugin/timezone/index.js defines the static `d.tz(input, timezone)` function. Currently it always treats `input` as a wall-clock local time string, which is wrong for non-string inputs (a numeric timestamp, a JS Date, or a Dayjs object). For those, the value is an absolute instant and must simply be converted to the target timezone.

STEP 1 (baseline, before editing): run `cd /dayjs && npx jest --coverage=false 2>&1 | tail -40` and save the summary (number of passing/failing suites and tests, names of failing tests).

STEP 2 (the edit): in /dayjs/src/plugin/timezone/index.js, change the body of `d.tz` from:

  d.tz = function (input, timezone) {
    const previousOffset = tzOffset(+d(), timezone)
    const localTs = d.utc(input).valueOf()

so that it reads:

  d.tz = function (input, timezone) {
    const previousOffset = tzOffset(+d(), timezone)
    if (typeof input !== 'string') {
      // timestamp, Date, Dayjs
      return d(input).tz(timezone)
    }
    const localTs = d.utc(input).valueOf()

Everything else in the file stays exactly as it is (including the rest of d.tz, proto.tz, fixOffset, tzOffset, d.tz.guess). Keep the file lint-clean: run `cd /dayjs && ./node_modules/.bin/eslint src/plugin/timezone/index.js` and report its output.

STEP 3 (verification): create a temporary test file /dayjs/test/plugin/zz-tmp-tzcheck.test.js with EXACTLY this content:

import MockDate from 'mockdate'
import moment from 'moment-timezone'
import dayjs from '../../src'
import utc from '../../src/plugin/utc'
import timezone from '../../src/plugin/timezone'

dayjs.extend(utc)
dayjs.extend(timezone)

beforeEach(() => { MockDate.set(new Date()) })
afterEach(() => { MockDate.reset() })

const NY = 'America/New_York'

it('parse timestamp, js Date, Day.js object', () => {
  const result = '2013-02-08T00:00:00-05:00'
  expect(dayjs.tz(1360306800000, NY).format()).toBe(result)
  expect(dayjs.tz(new Date(1360306800000), NY).format()).toBe(result)
  expect(dayjs.tz(dayjs(1360306800000), NY).format()).toBe(result)
  expect(dayjs.tz(1360306800000, NY).valueOf()).toBe(1360306800000)
  expect(dayjs.tz(1360306800000, NY).valueOf()).toBe(moment.tz(1360306800000, NY).valueOf())
  expect(dayjs.tz(new Date(1360306800000), NY).format()).toBe(moment.tz(new Date(1360306800000), NY).format())
  expect(dayjs.tz(dayjs(1360306800000), NY).format()).toBe(moment.tz(1360306800000, NY).format())
})

Then run it under several timezones and report the raw output of each:
  cd /dayjs && npx jest test/plugin/zz-tmp-tzcheck --coverage=false 2>&1 | tail -30
  cd /dayjs && TZ=Pacific/Auckland npx jest test/plugin/zz-tmp-tzcheck --coverage=false 2>&1 | tail -30
  cd /dayjs && TZ=Europe/London npx jest test/plugin/zz-tmp-tzcheck --coverage=false 2>&1 | tail -30
  cd /dayjs && TZ=America/Whitehorse npx jest test/plugin/zz-tmp-tzcheck --coverage=false 2>&1 | tail -30
If any assertion fails, report the exact failure message; do NOT weaken the test to make it pass, and do NOT change the source fix in a way that contradicts the instruction above (report instead).

STEP 4 (regression): run the full suite again: `cd /dayjs && npx jest --coverage=false 2>&1 | tail -40`, and also `cd /dayjs && TZ=Pacific/Auckland npx jest test/plugin/timezone.test --coverage=false 2>&1 | tail -20` and `cd /dayjs && TZ=Europe/London npx jest test/plugin/timezone.test --coverage=false 2>&1 | tail -20`. Compare with the STEP 1 baseline: no previously passing test may now fail.

STEP 5: DELETE the temporary file /dayjs/test/plugin/zz-tmp-tzcheck.test.js (rm it) and confirm with `ls /dayjs/test/plugin`. Leave the source fix in place.

FIX: in /dayjs/src/plugin/timezone/index.js, inside `proto.tz`, the line
    const diff = (this.toDate() - new Date(target)) / 1000 / 60
must become
    const diff = Math.round((this.toDate() - new Date(target)) / 1000 / 60)
(Only that one line changes. Leave the rest of the file - including the `d.tz` function which already contains an `if (typeof input !== 'string') { return d(input).tz(timezone) }` guard - untouched.)

VERIFY:
1. Create temp file /dayjs/test/plugin/zz-tz-z.test.js with EXACTLY:
import MockDate from 'mockdate'
import moment from 'moment-timezone'
import dayjs from '../../src'
import utc from '../../src/plugin/utc'
import timezone from '../../src/plugin/timezone'
dayjs.extend(utc)
dayjs.extend(timezone)
beforeEach(() => { MockDate.set(new Date()) })
afterEach(() => { MockDate.reset() })
it('Convert format Z', () => {
  expect(dayjs('2013-02-08T09:30:26.123').tz('America/New_York').format('Z')).toBe('-05:00')
  expect(dayjs('2013-02-08T09:30:26.123').tz('America/New_York').format('ZZ')).toBe('-0500')
  expect(dayjs('2013-02-08T09:30:26.123').tz('America/New_York').utcOffset()).toBe(-300)
  expect(dayjs('2013-02-08T09:30:26.123').tz('Asia/Tokyo').format('Z')).toBe('+09:00')
  expect(dayjs('2013-02-08T09:30:26.123').tz('America/New_York').format('Z')).toBe(moment('2013-02-08T09:30:26.123').tz('America/New_York').format('Z'))
  expect(dayjs('2014-06-01T12:00:00Z').tz('America/Los_Angeles').format()).toBe('2014-06-01T05:00:00-07:00')
})
2. Run: cd /dayjs && npx jest test/plugin/zz-tz-z --coverage=false 2>&1 | tail -25  -> must PASS.
3. Run the full suite: cd /dayjs && npx jest --coverage=false 2>&1 | tail -15 -> must be 56 suites / 524 tests passing (this is the known-good baseline in the default TZ).
4. Also run: cd /dayjs && TZ=Pacific/Auckland npx jest --coverage=false 2>&1 | tail -8 and TZ=Europe/London and TZ=America/Whitehorse; report the failing test NAMES in each. Known pre-existing baseline failures (must not grow): Auckland 7 failing tests (get-set 'Set Month and Year in last day of month', timezone 'parse target time string', timezone 'parse and convert between timezones', timezone 'convert to target time' x2, utc-utcOffset 'utc startOf', calendar 'ReferenceTime'); London 10; Whitehorse 6. Report exactly which tests fail now and compare.
5. Run cd /dayjs && ./node_modules/.bin/eslint src/plugin/timezone/index.js (must be clean).
6. Delete the temp file (rm /dayjs/test/plugin/zz-tz-z.test.js) and confirm `git status --short` shows only src/plugin/timezone/index.js modified.

FIX: /dayjs/src/locale/nl.js line 11 currently reads:
  ordinal: n => `${n}.`,
Change it to (moment.js-compatible Dutch ordinal):
  ordinal: n => `${n}${(n === 1 || n === 8 || n >= 20) ? 'ste' : 'de'}`,
Nothing else in the file changes.

import moment from 'moment'
import dayjs from '../../src'
import advancedFormat from '../../src/plugin/advancedFormat'
import '../../src/locale/nl'
dayjs.extend(advancedFormat)
it('Format Day of Month Do 1 - 31', () => {

    const d = `2018-05-${i < 10 ? `0${i}` : i}`
    expect(dayjs(d).locale('nl').format('Do')).toBe(moment(d).locale('nl').format('Do'))

const unitToMS = {
  years: MILLISECONDS_A_YEAR,
  months: MILLISECONDS_A_MONTH,
  days: MILLISECONDS_A_DAY,

  minutes: MILLISECONDS_A_MINUTE,
  seconds: MILLISECONDS_A_SECOND,
  weeks: MILLISECONDS_A_WEEK

to

  years: MILLISECONDS_A_YEAR,
  months: MILLISECONDS_A_MONTH,
